data.title: University Bancorp Closes on the Acquisition of 20% of UIF Corporation for Cash & Stock Worth About $15.2 Million
data.description:
ANN ARBOR, MI / ACCESS Newswire / October 30, 2026 / University Bancorp, Inc. (OTCQB:UNIB) or ("UNIB") announced that it closed today on the previously announced transaction to acquire 20% of UIF Corporation. UIF is a key subsidiary of University Bank, previously 80% owned, and now 100% owned by University Bank. The final terms at the closing of the transaction were different than the terms originally negotiated, which originally involved an all-stock stock swap.

In the transaction, UNIB issued 482,054 newly issued shares of UNIB common stock and in addition, paid $3,911,147.50 cash, to acquire the 20% of UIF that it did not already own. At September 30, 2026, UIF had shareholders' equity of $76,050,646. Minority Interest of $15,210,129 as of September 30, 2026 was acquired in the transaction. The acquisition therefore increases the shareholders' equity of UNIB by $11,298,981.70 as of September 30, 2026, had it closed then. The Tier 1 Capital of University Bank increases as a result of the acquisition by about $4 million going forward due to the elimination of the minority interest in UIF.

Shareholders and investors are encouraged to refer to the financial information including the investor presentations, audited financial statements, strategic plan and prior press releases, available on our investor relations web page at: http://www.university-bank.com/bancorp/.

A detailed income statement, balance sheet and other financial information for UNIB and University Bank as of September 30, 2026, is available here: https://www.university-bank.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/3Q2026-UNIB-Detailed-Financial-Information.pdf.

University Bancorp's most recent quarterly earnings press release is available here: https://www.university-bank.com/2026/10/22/university-bancorp-3q2026-net-income-4919946-09-0-95-per-share/.

University Bank's and Bank of Whittier's FDIC Quarterly Call Reports, with substantial additional information including loan origination, loan investment composition, delinquency ratios and Tier 1 Capital ratios for September 30, 2026, will be available by October 30, 2026 here: https://cdr.ffiec.gov/public/ManageFacsimiles.aspx

About UNIB

Ann Arbor-based University Bancorp is a Federal Reserve regulated financial holding company that owns:

  • 100% of University Bank, a bank based in Ann Arbor, Michigan;
  • 100% of Bank of Whittier, N.A., a bank located in Whittier, California;
  • 100% of Crescent Assurance, PCC, a captive insurance company licensed in Washington DC; and
  • 100% of Hyrex Servicing, a master mortgage servicing firm, based in Ann Arbor, Michigan.

University Bank together with its Michigan-based subsidiaries, holds and manages a total of over $36 billion in financial assets for over 185,000 customers, and our 550 employees make us the 5th largest bank based in Michigan. University Bank is an FDIC-insured, locally owned and managed community bank, and meets the financial needs of its community through its quality, creative and innovative services. Founded in 1890, University Bank® is the 15th oldest bank headquartered in Michigan. We are proud to have been selected as the "Community Bankers of the Year" by American Banker magazine, as the recipient of the American Bankers Association's Community Bank Award and as the recipient of USA Today's Top Workplace Award for several years in a row. University Bank is a Member FDIC. The members of University Bank's corporate family, ranked by their size of revenues are:

  • UIF, a faith-based banking firm based in Southfield, MI;
  • University Lending Group, a retail residential mortgage originator based in Clinton Township, MI;
  • Midwest Loan Services, a residential mortgage subservicer based in Houghton, MI;
  • Community Banking, based in Ann Arbor, MI, which provides traditional community banking services and wealth management;
  • Ann Arbor Insurance Centre, an independent insurance agency based in Ann Arbor, MI.
  • Mortgage Warehouse Lending, a mortgage warehouse lender based in Southfield, MI.

Hims & Hers Health and certain of its executives are charged with failing to disclose material information during the Class Period, violating federal securities laws.

On July 29, 2026, during market hours, the Federal Trade Commission ("FTC") announced that it had filed a lawsuit against the Company "alleging that the telehealth provider shared consumers' sensitive health information about medical conditions with third-party advertising platforms despite claiming its services maintain consumers' privacy and deceives users about its billing and cancellation practices." On this news, the price of Hims & Hers Health shares fell $4.32, or 14.73%, to close at $25.00 on July 29, 2026, on unusually heavy trading volume.

data.title: Fitch Cuts France's Outlook to Negative on Weaker Growth, Widening Deficit — Update
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis 




  Fitch Ratings lowered its outlook on France's credit rating to negative from stable, as the country faces economic and social pressure over its debt and growing borrowing costs. 



  Fitch said the negative outlook reflects a deterioration since its August review, and cited weaker growth, higher borrowing costs and a wider deficit. These factors are worsening debt dynamics from an already weak starting point, Fitch added. 



  Yields on France's government bonds have also risen since the last review, Fitch said. The agency said it now forecasts interest payments will increase to 3.3% of GDP in 2028 from 2.5% of GDP in 2025. Fitch also sees France's deficit at 5.5% of GDP in 2027, which it said reflects a weaker growth assessment and the risk of concessions during the budget process. 



  The next scheduled review date for France's rating hasn't yet been set, Fitch said, but added it expects to review the rating by end-February 2027 at the latest. 



  France's public debt is closing on 120% of its GDP, and the nation's economy shrank in the third quarter. The government is expecting the deficit to hit 5.4% of GDP this year. 



  In recent weeks, hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets of Paris and other French cities, with some protesters resorting to vandalism and violence. 



  Right-wing presidential candidate Marine Le Pen has recently cast herself as a unifying figure, and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has vowed to cancel hundreds of billions of euros in French national debt, The Wall Street Journal reported. 



  Last week, Moody's Ratings kept its Aa3 credit rating on France unchanged, citing the country's diversified economy and strong public institutions. However, Moody's retained its negative outlook on the country as France continues to face political instability and protests. 



  Moody's retains a higher rating than peers Fitch and S&P Global Ratings. S&P had lowered France's rating to A+ in October of last year. 



  Fitch affirmed the country's A+ rating, which it said is supported by a large, wealthy and diversified economy, strong institutions, euro area membership and a resilient banking sector.

data.title: /C O R R E C T I O N - PG&E Corporation/
data.description:
Five California Nonprofits Receive $500,000 to Restore Habitats, Expand Environmental Education and Strengthen Local Food Systems

Five California Nonprofits Receive $500,000 to Restore Habitats, Expand Environmental Education and Strengthen Local Food Systems

PR Newswire

OAKLAND, Calif., Oct. 30, 2026

Final round of PG&E Corporation Foundation grants completes a five-year, $2.5 million investment in 25 community organizations

Link to the B-roll and soundbite from Sacramento Splash

OAKLAND, Calif., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The PG&E Corporation Foundation (PG&E Foundation) is awarding five community-based organizations in Northern and Central California a total of $500,000 in grants for local initiatives dedicated to environmental stewardship.

The 2026 grant recipients represent the program's final group, completing the PG&E Foundation's five-year investment in projects that help strengthen local ecosystems and communities.

Since its launch in 2022, the Better Together Nature Positive Innovation Grant Program has invested $2.5 million in 25 organizations across Pacific Gas and Electric Company's (PG&E) service area, advancing environmental stewardship and supporting community-led innovation.

The five organizations will each receive $100,000 through the Better Together Nature Positive Innovation Grant program for leading efforts to preserve California's unique biodiversity, focusing on land, air quality and water stewardship.

Funding for this initiative comes from PG&E shareholders, not customers.

"For 27 years, Sacramento Splash has helped kids connect with the natural world through hands-on science and environmental education. Thanks to PG&E's support, about 7,000 students will experience Project Agriculture, Water, Energy & Environment during the 2026–27 school year, learning where their food comes from and how everyday choices can help create a more sustainable future," said Mackenzie Wieser, Chief Executive Officer, Sacramento Splash.

"We extend our sincere gratitude to all the organizations, partners and community leaders who helped make this program a success. What inspires us most is seeing local organizations turn their deep understanding of their communities into meaningful action, creating lasting impact where it matters most," said Carla Peterman, President, PG&E Corporation, and Chair of The PG&E Corporation Foundation Board.

Grant recipients are based in each of PG&E's five regions: North Coast; North Valley and Sierra; Bay Area; South Bay and Central Coast; and Central Valley. Receiving grants are:

  • Noyo Center: Kelp Forest Recovery (Fort Bragg) - Noyo Center restores Mendocino Coast kelp forests by removing invasive urchins and planting bull kelp. The project also supports red abalone recovery and environmental education. These efforts help create healthier, more resilient coastal ecosystems.
  • Sacramento Splash (Sacramento) - Project Agriculture, Water, Energy & Environment gives students in grades 2-5 from underserved Sacramento County schools hands-on learning experiences at the Historic Nicolaus Dairy in Elk Grove, often providing their first opportunity to visit a working farm. Students explore agriculture and environmental stewardship by planting and harvesting crops, building compost, observing bees, and learning about water conservation. Grant funding will support educators, transportation for Title I schools, and educational materials, helping the program reach approximately 7,000 students from 231 classes during the 2026-27 school year.
  • Friends of Sausal Creek (Oakland) - Friends of Sausal Creek will expand its paid youth stewardship program to provide year-round green job skills training for Oakland youth while helping restore the 2,600-acre Sausal Creek watershed. Participants will gain hands-on experience through habitat restoration, water quality improvements, and kayak-based estuary cleanups. In Jingletown, youth will also design and install a native planting plan and help create a community interpretive sign.
  • Point Blue Conservation Science (Bolinas) - Point Blue Conservation Science's program gives K-12 students hands-on experience restoring natural habitats while learning about environmental stewardship. In San Benito County, students, community college interns, residents, and land stewards will work with local partners to plant native vegetation and restore streamside habitat along an important wildlife corridor. The project will improve water quality, wildlife habitat, and climate resilience while providing students with education, job training and career development opportunities in conservation.
  • Black Urban Farmers Association (Stockton) – Black Urban Farmers Association (BUFA) has operated a pesticide-free urban farm in Stockton since 2015, providing fresh food and promoting regenerative farming. The project will help BUFA expand to a permanent one-acre site with more green space, education, and sustainable agriculture opportunities. Grant funding will support site planning, environmental reviews, infrastructure, and a community launch, strengthening long-term food security and environmental stewardship.

With the selection of the 2026 grantees, the application period has closed and the Better Together Nature Positive Innovation Grant Program is no longer accepting applications.

About PG&E
Pacific Gas and Electric Company, a subsidiary of PG&E Corporation (NYSE:PCG), is a combined natural gas and electric utility serving more than 16 million people across 70,000 square miles in Northern and Central California. For more information, visit pge.com and pge.com/news.

About The PG&E Corporation Foundation
The PG&E Corporation Foundation is an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization, separate from PG&E and sponsored by PG&E Corporation.

Twilio Investigation Notice: Levi & Korsinsky Notifies Investors of Pending Investigation Into Twilio (TWLO)

PR Newswire

NEW YORK, Oct. 30, 2026

Twilio's CFO told analysts "we're not seeing a slowdown" and its CEO later cited "accelerating revenue growth." The Company has now guided fourth-quarter organic growth to 11% to 12%, and shares fell as much as 17%. The investigation focuses on whether Twilio's growth disclosures met federal securities law requirements.

NEW YORK, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- After Twilio Inc. (NYSE: TWLO) guided organic revenue growth down from 16% to as low as 11% in its third-quarter report, its shares fell as much as 17%. Investors holding losses from that decline have legal rights. Shareholders who lost money are encouraged to submit their Twilio loss details now or to contact Joseph E. Levi, Esq. at jlevi@levikorsinsky.com or (212) 363-7500.

Management had addressed growth directly on earlier earnings calls. On May 1, 2025, CFO Aidan Viggiano answered an analyst: "No, we're not seeing a slowdown, Mark." On February 12, 2026, CEO Khozema Shipchandler said: "Reflecting on 2025, Twilio stood out with accelerating revenue growth, expanding operating margins and by delivering significant growth in free cash flow." The new fourth-quarter outlook sits 4 to 5 percentage points below the 16% organic growth the Company just reported. Management's commentary pointed to slowing growth in its largest business.

Levi & Korsinsky is investigating potential securities law violations. The investigation focuses on whether Twilio may not have adequately disclosed the growth trend in its largest business. It also examines whether the Company's public statements met the disclosure standards that federal securities laws require of public companies.

If you lost money on Twilio stock, request a free review of your TWLO losses or call (212) 363-7500.

WHY LEVI & KORSINSKY -- Ranked in ISS Securities Class Action Services' Top 50 Report for seven consecutive years, Levi & Korsinsky, LLP is a nationally recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation. With a team of over 70 professionals, the firm has recovered hundreds of millions of dollars for investors.

Frequently Asked Questions About the TWLO Investigation

Q: Who is eligible to participate in the TWLO investigation?A: Investors who purchased TWLO stock or securities and suffered financial losses may be eligible. Eligibility is based on purchase date and documented losses -- not on whether you still hold the shares.

Q: How much did TWLO stock drop?A: Shares fell more than 17%. The decline came after the Company disclosed fourth-quarter guidance calling for 11% to 12% organic revenue growth, down from 16% in the third quarter. Investors who purchased shares at allegedly inflated prices and suffered losses may be eligible to seek compensation.

Q: Which statements are being investigated as potentially misleading?A: The investigation concerns whether Twilio made materially false or misleading statements about its revenue growth trajectory, including growth in its largest business. When the Company disclosed fourth-quarter guidance of 11% to 12% organic revenue growth, the stock price declined sharply.

Q: What do TWLO investors need to do right now?A: Investors may gather brokerage records showing purchase dates, share quantities, and prices paid. Submit your information for a no-cost, no-obligation evaluation of your potential recovery. No immediate action is required to remain eligible to participate in the investigation.

Q: What is a lead plaintiff and why does it matter?A: If the investigation proceeds to legal action, a lead plaintiff is the investor the court appoints to represent the group of affected investors. Lead plaintiffs are typically investors with the largest documented losses. Contacting the firm during the investigation phase preserves that option.

Q: What if I already sold my TWLO shares -- can I still recover losses?A: Yes. Eligibility is based on when you purchased, not whether you still hold the shares. Investors who bought TWLO and sold at a loss may still participate in the investigation.

Q: Do I need to go to court or give testimony?A: No. Participating in the investigation does not require court appearances or depositions. If legal action is later pursued, the overwhelming majority of affected investors never appear in court either.

Q: What does it cost me to participate?A: There is no upfront cost to submit your information and review whether you may be eligible to recover. Should you choose to participate in any resulting action, these matters are generally handled on a contingency basis, with any attorneys' fees and expenses subject to court approval.
